speaker: Narrator
exact_quote: John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness.
greek: ἐγένετο Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ
scene_action: Adult John the Baptist appears alone beside the Jordan.
caption: John the Baptist appears in the wilderness
parallel: Matthew 3:1–6 · Luke 3:1–6; later Synoptic reuse is not independent
note: Mark begins with the adult John; no birth story is narrated.

speaker: Narrator
exact_quote: They were being baptized by him in the Jordan River.
greek: ἐβαπτίζοντο ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ
scene_action: John baptizes people while others walk toward the Jordan.
caption: The people go out to John at the Jordan
historical_status: Core John tradition; parallels not three independent votes
note: Matthew and Luke preserve related scenes but both use Mark in the dominant scholarly model.

speaker: John the Baptist
exact_quote: The one stronger than me is coming after me.
greek: Ἔρχεται ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου ὀπίσω μου
scene_action: John publicly points beyond himself toward the coming one.
caption: John points beyond himself
historical_status: Widely attested John tradition; sources are not fully independent
note: All four Gospels preserve the coming-one motif, with different wording and framing.

speaker: John the Baptist
exact_quote: I baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.
greek: ἐγὼ ἐβάπτισα ὑμᾶς ὕδατι, αὐτὸς δὲ βαπτίσει ὑμᾶς ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ
scene_action: John contrasts the water in his hand with the coming work of Spirit.
caption: Water opens toward Spirit
historical_status: Early shared tradition; Matthew and Luke add fire
note: Mark has Holy Spirit; the authors of Matthew and Luke add ‘and fire.’

speaker: Narrator
exact_quote: Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee.
greek: ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲτ τῆς Γαλιλαίας
scene_action: Jesus walks through the shallows toward John.
caption: Jesus comes from Nazareth to the Jordan
historical_status: Earliest narrative bridge from John to Jesus
note: Mark moves directly from John's proclamation to Jesus' arrival.

speaker: Narrator
exact_quote: He was baptized in the Jordan by John.
greek: ἐβαπτίσθη εἰς τὸν Ἰορδάνην ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου
scene_action: John directly baptizes Jesus in the Jordan.
caption: John the Baptist baptizes Jesus
historical_status: Core historical tradition with later narrative reframing
note: Mark names John as the baptizer and narrates no objection.

speaker: John the Baptist
exact_quote: I need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?
greek: Ἐγὼ χρείαν ἔχω ὑπὸ σοῦ βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ σὺ ἔρχῃ πρός με;
scene_action: John raises his hand and tries to prevent Jesus.
caption: John objects to baptizing Jesus
certainty: Matthew-only dialogue added to Mark's scene
historical_status: Later authorial redaction, not a scribal variant
note: The author of Matthew adds John's objection; it is absent from the earlier Markan account.

speaker: Jesus
scene_action: Jesus answers; John lowers his resistance and accepts.
caption: Jesus asks John to allow it now
certainty: Matthew-only dialogue added to Mark's scene
historical_status: Later authorial explanation, not a scribal variant
note: The author of Matthew adds Jesus' reply to explain the baptism; it is absent from Mark.

speaker: Narrator
exact_quote: Jesus was baptized and was praying.
scene_action: Jesus prays after baptism; John is deliberately absent from the frame.
caption: Luke lets the baptizer recede
historical_status: Passive report; baptizer unnamed in this scene
note: The author of Luke places John's imprisonment first, then reports Jesus' baptism passively without naming the baptizer.

speaker: John the Baptist
exact_quote: I saw the Spirit descending like a dove from heaven, and it remained on him.
greek: Τεθέαμαι τὸ πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον ὡς περιστερὰν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐπ’ αὐτόν
scene_action: John points to Jesus and testifies; no immersion is shown.
caption: John becomes the witness
historical_status: Baptism recalled as witness; immersion not narrated
note: The Fourth Gospel does not narrate the immersion; it recasts John as the witness who sees the Spirit descend and remain.
